## 29. STATIC KEEP-OUT ZONES — full BUILD → TUNE → TIGHTEN arc (extends §20)

The §20 collision foundation became a real per-cell STATIC keep-out feature this session, with several honest iterations driven by what showed on screen:

### 29a. Architecture confirmed (reading the deployed code)
- `static_zones.py` (in the `cobot_dashboard` package) is well-built: loads the cell's saved `baseline_cloud.pcd`, voxel-downsamples, crops to the 1.4m reach cylinder, drops the robot self-footprint, ground-extracts (RANSAC), DBSCAN-clusters (reuses `lidar_object_identifier` GroundExtractor / ObjectClusterer / shape_analyzer.analyze — NO rewrite), fits OBB per cluster, density/volume-filters, **union-find MERGES** overlapping/near AABBs (one bench = one box), inflates by margin, persists `collision_zones.json` + a MoveIt2 PlanningScene sidecar (`planning_scene_collision_objects.json`, frame_id base_link, BOX primitives) for future planning. Endpoints: POST `/api/cells/{id}/collision_zones/build`, GET/DELETE `/api/cells/{id}/collision_zones`, GET `/api/collision/static_zones`. Frame: baseline cloud is in livox_frame which collision_monitor + 3D viewer treat as base_link → static boxes share the live LiDAR-box frame.
- 3D rendering exists: `CollisionScene3D` (ArmViewer3D) + `CollisionOverlay.jsx` render the boxes; a `StaticZonesToggle` (default ON) shows/hides them.

### 29b. "No boxes" → root cause = build never triggered / no baseline
- Zones were MANUAL-only (POST build) and nothing auto-ran them. First "active cell" tested (Test, 0f466261e4fb) had `baseline_captured:false`, 0 points, NO pcd — so build correctly returned `{ok:false, reason:'no_baseline'}` and the empty 3D view was correct behavior, not a bug.
- **FIX: auto-build hook** — after a baseline is captured/recaptured in the Setup Wizard, `build_zones_from_pcd` + `save_zones` run automatically (best-effort; failures logged, don't block the wizard). `GET /api/cells/{id}/baseline/status` now includes `zones_built`/`zones_error`. So a freshly commissioned cell already has zones with no manual click.

### 29c. GIANT box bug #1 — no max-size rejection (floor boxed as one obstacle)
- After capture, a GIANT box labeled "static obstacle · 0 mm" enclosed nearly the whole reach volume, beside one correct small box. Root cause: the floor/ground RANSAC didn't fully remove a thin sheet, DBSCAN chained it into ONE workspace-spanning cluster, and there was NO upper-size limit. The "0 mm" distance = origin-centered enormous box = the tell.
- **FIX (added to static_zones DEFAULTS, logged into diag['rejected'] / ['merged_rejected']):** `max_obstacle_xy_m=0.9`, `max_footprint_frac=0.40` (reject if footprint > 40% of the reach disc = it's the floor), `flat_z_max_m`/flat-wide-sheet rejection, plus a `ground_clearance_m=0.03` cull above the fitted plane (drops the 200–300 residual floor points RANSAC's 1.5cm band missed). Applied at BOTH per-cluster and post-merge stages. Result: n_zones 2 → 1 (giant phantom gone). Pushed c311fab.

### 29d. OVERSIZED boxes #2 — AABB-not-OBB + outlier-stretched extents
- Boxes were still loose — enclosing big empty volume, not hugging clusters; giant "0 mm" box reappeared in the live/keep-out render. Two structural causes diagnosed from the code:
  1. **`static_zones` deliberately emits AXIS-ALIGNED boxes (AABB) with identity orientation** (for the collision_monitor capsule-vs-AABB check) — an AABB around a rotated/diagonal object is far bigger than the object. THIS is the core looseness.
  2. **`shape_analyzer._principal_axes` uses raw min/max extents on the PCA projection** — a single outlier point stretches the OBB across empty space (no percentile trimming / outlier rejection).
- **FIX direction prescribed:** use TIGHT ORIENTED boxes (store the OBB rotation quaternion, render the OBB the viewer already supports) instead of AABB; compute extents from PERCENTILES (2nd–98th) not raw min/max + statistical outlier removal before fitting; reduce `inflate_margin_m` (0.05→0.02–0.03); tighten `merge_gap_m` (0.05→0.01–0.02) to stop over-merging separate objects; reject merged groups that balloon past the max-size limits. NOTE: collision_monitor's capsule-vs-box math may need updating to handle oriented boxes — flagged as a tradeoff (AABB is simpler for the capsule check; OBB is correct for tightness/visualization).
- **CRITICAL OPERATIONAL LESSON reinforced:** zones only regenerate on REBUILD (POST .../collision_zones/build or recapture) — a code change + dashboard restart does NOT change the persisted `collision_zones.json`. Several "fix didn't take" moments were stale saved zones and/or stale browser bundle. Always: rebuild zones AND hard-refresh.

### 29e. Banner / labels
- "Baseline cloud failed to load — check the Setup Wizard" banner appeared WITH boxes present → boxes (from collision_zones.json) and the baseline cloud (fetch of `/api/cells/{id}/baseline/cloud`) were OUT OF SYNC: zones existed for a cell whose baseline PCD wouldn't load (active cell changed, or PCD missing/moved, or endpoint erroring). Diagnostic prompt prescribed the curl checks (active id → baseline/cloud status 200/404/500 → PCD exists on disk?) and to RECONCILE rather than just hide the banner.
- "static obstacle · NNN mm" floating labels: repeatedly asked to remove (3×). The `<Html>` label in CollisionOverlay (~line 112-127) is gated by `showLabel`; fix = `showLabel && !isBaselineStatic` so static keep-out boxes render NO label (keep boxes; keep live dynamic labels). Repeated reappearance strongly attributed to BROWSER BUNDLE CACHING — hard-refresh + confirm new bundle hash before judging.

## 30. 3D-VIEW CLOUD DENSITY + "SUPER LIGHT" CLOUD (extends §22)
- The 3D View renders the active cell's SAVED baseline (voxel-downsampled), which looks sparse vs the dense LIVE cloud on Cameras & LiDAR — different sources by design. Fixes prescribed: raise the baseline fetch budget toward `LIDAR_MAX_PTS` (131072) instead of `max_points=80000`, increase `pointsMaterial size` 0.006→~0.012–0.015, and reduce server-side voxel so the returned baseline keeps tens of thousands of points; if the saved PCD itself is sparse, RECAPTURE with `roboai-fusion` stopped (the §21 degrade-to-80-pts service). The diag's `n_after_voxel` distinguishes a sparse capture from an over-aggressive filter.
- "Only one box" was diagnosed as possibly CORRECT (only one real obstacle in reach, floor correctly rejected) — read the diag (n_clusters_raw vs n_clusters_kept) before loosening thresholds; don't tune blindly.

## 31. MIRRORED-SCENE BUG — handedness in ROS→Three conversion (root cause found in code)
- The LiDAR scene rendered MIRRORED. Root cause read directly from `LidarPanel.jsx` (and the same in `ArmViewer3D` BaselineCloudInScene): the ROS Z-up → Three Y-up conversion is a PLAIN axis swap `(x, y, z) → (x, z, y)` with NO negation, which FLIPS HANDEDNESS (right-handed ROS → left-handed result = mirror). 
- **FIX:** negate one axis to preserve handedness — `(x, y, z) → (x, z, -y)`. Apply the SAME corrected mapping EVERYWHERE it's inlined (LidarPanel cloud loops ~63-65/81-83/95-97, trail ~209-212, DetectionMarkers/marker map ~351-352/437-439, and ArmViewer3D BaselineCloudInScene) so points, boxes, scene objects, trails, and keep-out zones all agree (otherwise boxes float off clusters). Acceptance test: a KNOWN left-side object must appear on the left (verify with a real asymmetric landmark, not by eye). Likely also contributed to earlier "boxes don't hug clusters" confusion.

Empty states: "Not taught yet. Use the Teach button on the row, or 'Use current pose' above." Full TeachOverlay with jog pad exists.
- So the model the user asked for (auto-populate + linked-but-overridable + manual reteach) is present. Prescribed work = VERIFY it shows on every move step in BOTH wizard-generated AND PBD-draft programs, surface the Teach affordance at ROW level if buried, and ensure no pose-bearing step type is missing the button (extend TEACHABLE_ACTIONS / fix isTeachable for any gap). Editor persists via PUT /api/programs/{id}; executor reads updated poses.

## 33. LOAD-PROGRAM DROPDOWN — z-index / clipping / click-intercept
- In the Program tab, the "Load" saved-programs dropdown didn't function or rendered BEHIND the page. Root cause in ProgramEditor.jsx (~line 2171): the dropdown is `position:absolute` with `zIndex:21` while other overlays use 1000–9999, and absolute positioning lets a parent `overflow:hidden`/stacking context clip it.
- **FIX:** render the dropdown via a React PORTAL to document.body with `position:fixed` at the button's getBoundingClientRect coords, at a high z-index above page chrome (e.g. 4000/4001), keep the click-outside backdrop. DIAGNOSE the "does not function" half: if `showLoadMenu` flips true but nothing shows → clipping/z-index; if state never flips → an invisible element is intercepting the click above the button.

## 34. PROGRAM-LIBRARY TAB-SWITCH STALENESS (same family as the active-cell sync)
- Switching to Program Library sometimes shows an incomplete list that "catches up" after a delay. Root cause: tabs UNMOUNT on switch (per useStore comment) and ProgramLibrary fetches `/api/programs` on mount (`useEffect(()=>load(),[load])`); the user sees stale/empty state until the fetch resolves, and a just-saved program may not appear immediately.
- **FIX:** show a LOADING state on mount (not stale/empty), make the list authoritative on each visit, and ELIMINATE the save→library lag by updating a shared Zustand programs slice immediately on save (optimistic add / refetch-on-save) so Library reads one source of truth. Same class of bug as the active-cell sync (§ v17) — durable answer is store-backed data with a single fetch action that both mount and save call.

## 35. SETUP WIZARD / CONFIGURE — ACTIVE-CELL AUTO-DEFAULT + tab-refetch (extends v17 §18)
- 3D View showed "No active cell — pick one in Configure" even when a cell was active; Configure's cell list didn't populate until a manual refresh. Same root family: components read/write different state and only fetch once on mount.
- **FIX deployed:** `hydrateActiveCell()` — 3D View resolves the active cell from a shared store value, falling back to GET `/api/cells/active`, on mount AND tab-focus; brief "Loading active cell…" chip then the active cell's baseline cloud + a "Baseline · <name> · N pts · <ts>" chip; distinct messages for truly-no-active-cell vs active-cell-has-no-baseline. Configure cells list made store-driven so it loads without manual refresh. Verified: `curl /api/cells/active` returns the activated cell; a real capture (cell 34052ab0952b) reported ~37,437-point baseline. **Recurring caveat:** if FE state lags the backend, HARD-REFRESH — several "still not working" reports were stale cached bundles, not code.

## 37. LiDAR MESH / LIVOX VIEWER 2 — will NOT boost cloud quality
- Teddy uploaded LivoxViewer2 for Ubuntu v2.3.0 (x86-64 desktop app, ~191MB) and asked if it boosts LiDAR mesh quality. **Answer: no.** It's a Livox device VISUALIZATION/CONFIGURATION tool (live cloud view, device settings, .lvx record/playback) — it only DISPLAYS the same data the `livox_ros_driver2` already delivers; it adds zero points and won't run on the ARM64 Jetson (x86 only — runs on a laptop). The real levers for density/mesh quality are the accumulator settings (already took sparse → ~37k–66k pts) and WIRING nvblox into the dashboard (built but dormant per §24); the MID-360 is fundamentally a coarse environment/safety scanner, not a fine-detail sensor (fine geometry = the MotionCam's job). Livox Viewer 2's legitimate use = a laptop-side DIAGNOSTIC to check whether the sensor itself is healthy independent of the ROS2/dashboard stack.

## 38. BIN PICKING + MOTION PLANNING WITH THE MOTIONCAM — honest difficulty framing
- Asked if bin picking + motion planning with the Photoneo MotionCam will be EASY. **Honest answer: no — bin picking is among the hardest problems in industrial robotics; the MotionCam being excellent hardware doesn't change that.** What the MotionCam makes easier: the SENSING half (dense 0.5mm clouds, PSL continuous-during-motion, good on shiny/dark parts that defeated the D435i) — it removes the sensor bottleneck behind the earlier recognition struggles. What stays hard regardless of camera: recognition + 6DOF pose in CLUTTER (overlap/occlusion; the MD's delrin-vs-BT225 saga; months-to-production not weeks), GRASP planning (which face/approach, gripper fit, stability), collision-aware MOTION PLANNING (in/out of a deep bin without hitting walls/parts/self — needs MoveIt2 + a planning scene, BLOCKED on the official Estun URDF/DH pending the arm), and the LONG TAIL (near-empty bin, tangled parts, failure recovery, cycle time). Realistic timeline: a controlled DEMO in weeks once camera+arm integrated; PRODUCTION-reliable on real parts = months of iteration on real bins. Buildable NOW toward this (no camera): the CAD→model recognition reference side from STEP files (~30-40%), and MoveIt2 setup once the arm's DH table is pulled from the teach pendant.

## 39. PHOTONEO SDK / DRIVER / ARM64 DUE DILIGENCE — the decisive pre-purchase question

### 39a. Do we need Photoneo's driver? — yes for acquisition, no for the intelligence
- You MUST use Photoneo software to GET a point cloud — the camera is closed: it projects patterns and runs Photoneo's PROPRIETARY PSL reconstruction internally; there's no documented raw protocol to write your own driver against (unlike RealSense's open `librealsense` or Livox's open `livox_ros_driver2`, which is exactly why NeuRobots could write its own software for those). 
- Two layers: **PhoXi Control** = Photoneo's core software/engine that operates the camera and produces the cloud (available BOTH as a desktop GUI for setup/diagnostics AND as an SDK/API your code calls); the **ROS2 wrapper (`phoxi_camera`)** sits on top to expose clouds as ROS2 topics.
- **The architecture mirrors the current sensors exactly:** PhoXi Control's SDK is just a (better) camera driver in the SAME slot as librealsense/livox — `cloud = capture()` returns an (N,3)(+color+normals) array, and EVERYTHING above that is NeuRobots's own software (PPF+ICP recognition, FoundationPose pose, grasp selection, MoveIt2 planning, dashboard). Photoneo never sees/trains-on/constrains that pipeline.

### 39b. Can we write our own software like for the cameras/LiDAR? — above the SDK yes, the driver itself no
- The bottom layer (device comms + PSL reconstruction) is CLOSED IP — cannot be self-written/replaced. Everything ABOVE the cloud is yours, and you CAN write your own thin ROS2 WRAPPER on top of PhoXi Control's SDK (e.g. if the official phoxi_camera ROS2 node doesn't support ARM64 but the SDK does).
- **Photoneo confirmed** that many of their customers build their own custom software on top of their hardware — which validates the software ARCHITECTURE (custom pipeline on the SDK) but does NOT by itself confirm the PLATFORM (most such customers run x86 industrial PCs, not ARM64 Jetson).

### 39c. Runs LOCALLY — yes; the open question is WHICH machine
- PhoXi Control runs entirely LOCALLY (no cloud service, no internet, camera over local Ethernet — same local pattern as librealsense/livox on the Jetson today). The unresolved qualifier is whether it runs locally ON THE JETSON (ARM64) or needs a local x86 helper PC that forwards the cloud to the Jetson over the LAN. Either way data stays local/private; it's one box vs two.

### 39d. THE decisive pre-purchase question + email drafted
- **Make-or-break: does PhoXi Control / the SDK run on ARM64 (aarch64), specifically the Jetson AGX Orin under JetPack 6 / Ubuntu 22.04?** If yes → runs on the Jetson, write your own ROS2 wrapper + full pipeline on top. If x86-only → need an x86 machine in the loop (architecture impact). This remains the single biggest MotionCam unknown (carried from v16).
- **Two questions distilled for Teddy to ask Photoneo:** (1) Does PhoXi Control/SDK run on ARM64 — specifically Jetson AGX Orin on JetPack 6; if x86-only, say so directly. (2) Does the SDK/API give direct access to the raw point cloud (xyz+color+normals) to run our own recognition/pose software, with NO requirement to use Photoneo Locator/their application software?
- An email to Photoneo was drafted (two variants: thorough "Confirm SDK + ARM64" and "Short/direct") confirming the custom-software-on-SDK understanding and nailing the ARM64/JetPack-6/Jetson question, plus SKU (MotionCam-3D Color S+), inclusions (lens/cables/PSU/PhoXi Control license perpetual-vs-time-limited/warranty), official ROS2 Humble wrapper vs self-written, minimum settle time after motion for wrist-mount capture, and PoE powering. **STATUS: ARM64/Jetson answer PENDING — gates the purchase commitment.**

## 41. PROCESS LESSONS — JUNE 17 ADDITIONS (extend §27/§13; all prior lessons still govern)
13. **Browser bundle CACHING masks fixes.** The day's most repeated trap: a fix was built+deployed but the browser/tablet served the OLD bundle, so it "still didn't work." ALWAYS hard-refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R / clear tablet cache) and confirm the served JS hash changed BEFORE concluding a fix failed. Multiple "still broken" reports were stale bundles, not code.
14. **Know which BRANCH (and path) is the source of truth.** Stale ZIPs came from `main` (Jun 10) while work lived on `feature/motion-lidar-step-foundation`. Verify the branch; verify the deployed path == the git repo path; verify a marker file is actually in the artifact before trusting it (date-check + grep for today's filenames).
15. **Persisted artifacts need REGENERATION, not just a code change.** Static zones live in `collision_zones.json` — editing static_zones.py + restarting does nothing until you REBUILD the zones (POST build / recapture). Distinguish "code path fixed" from "saved data regenerated."
16. **Handedness is not orientation.** A mirrored scene = a left/right-handed flip from a bare axis swap, fixed by negating one axis — not a camera-angle illusion. Verify with a known asymmetric landmark, and apply the SAME mapping to every layer (points, boxes, trails, zones) or they desync.
17. **Verify before building — features may already exist.** Reteach-on-move-steps was already fully implemented; the right move was verify-and-surface, not rebuild. Read the deployed code first.
18. **Name the closed-vs-open boundary precisely (Photoneo).** You can write everything ABOVE the point cloud (it's the same slot as your open RealSense/Livox drivers), but the acquisition+reconstruction layer is Photoneo's closed IP — and "runs locally" still leaves "on which machine (ARM64?)" as the decisive, separate question.
